items.title: Define issuer-bound agent-to-agent review authority
items.body:
## Outcome

Define and implement a reviewed, non-bypass path for one independently identifiable agent to review another agent's work, with an explicit policy transition from [ADR 0202](https://github.com/VerJSON/.github/tree/main/docs/decisions/0202-bind-autonomous-merge-to-independent-review-receipt). The organization owner intends distinct agents to review one another; labels, model names, or shared GitHub accounts alone do not establish that independence.

## Required outcome

- Distinguish advisory review evidence, a provider-recognized approval, and authority to perform a normal merge. Existing platform-required human, code-owner, and last-push approvals remain binding whenever applicable; no agent or App may supply a missing required human approval or bypass a ruleset.
- Bind author and reviewer to distinct issuer-verified agent principals and runs, exact repository, PR, head, base, diff/candidate, scope, policy version, expiry, nonce and revocation state. Define provider-action-to-signed-run correlation, non-self-review, replay protection and retained audit evidence. Do not infer independence from a GitHub account or model alias.
- Evaluate how an agent review can satisfy a dedicated deterministic check without claiming it is a native GitHub approval; separately prove any provider approval semantics before relying on them. Define a non-bypass merger identity and its separation or any explicitly reviewed exception.
- Bring the successor decision through the organization ARB/TDA/ATA process with complete pinned context and deterministic validation; preserve dissent, unresolved integration constraints and the current policy until the successor is approved. Coordinate identity-service and review-board implementations before claiming authority is deployed.
- Exercise forged or replayed proofs, same-agent and same-run reviews, revoked or stale policy, retargeted/base/head changes, provider actor ambiguity, unavailable issuer and platform approval enforcement.

## Context

Related work: VerJSON/verjson-agents#453, VerJSON/verjson-agent-identity#1, VerJSON/.github#1945, and the temporary protection exception VerJSON/.github#1933. The isolated queue canary confirms only PR-head check dispatch; it has not established agent approval, merge-group behavior or production readiness.

items.body:
_Opened by Claude Code from #60 SEC-7 (security review of #52). Owner asked for this issue on 2026-10-15._

## Goal
Make "the agent never pushes to or merges into `main`" something GitHub enforces, not just the hard rule plus best-effort backstops.

Today the agent uses the owner's account, which has the ruleset admin bypass. #60 showed that command-text deny patterns and the `pre-push` hook can be beaten by shell quoting (`git push --no\-verify …` pushed `main` on a scratch repo). That residual risk is accepted for now (threat model, AI-agent row).

## Options (owner decides)
- **Bot account** (second GitHub user, write access, not in the ruleset bypass list) with a fine-grained PAT limited to this repo.
- **GitHub App** installed on the repo, with contents/PR write, outside the bypass list; tokens minted locally.

Either way: the agent's `gh`/git credentials use that identity; the owner keeps the bypass; `production` deploy approval stays owner-only.

## Scope
- [ ] Owner: create the identity and token (agent can't)
- [ ] Docs: how the agent session gets the token (env var, never in the repo), `docs/ops/` or CLAUDE.md
- [ ] Threat model: update the AI-agent row and the revisit trigger; ROADMAP owner setup step 1
- [ ] Decide whether the deny list / hook stay as defence in depth (recommended)

Touches CLAUDE.md workflow rules and `.claude/` → security reviewer.

items.title: security: review main ruleset approval and bypass policy
items.body:
## Current state (rechecked 2026-10-25)

The active `main` ruleset requires these status checks:
- Offline regression and evaluator suites
- Gitleaks secret scan
- Parse workflow and Dependabot YAML
- tests
- Python static security analysis
- Dependency vulnerability audit

PR #39 was merged after all PR checks passed. It removes path filters from the isolated security workflow's `pull_request` trigger, so docs-only PRs will still report the required security contexts. Push-to-main remains path-filtered to reduce duplicate runs.

## Remaining policy risks
1. `required_approving_review_count: 0`: no independent review is required before merge.
2. A repository-role bypass actor uses `bypass_mode: always`, allowing bypass of the ruleset.
3. `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`: the branch does not require the PR head to be up to date with `main` before merge.

## Recommended changes
- Require at least one independent approval if compatible with the solo-maintainer workflow; otherwise document the intentional exception and rely on an independent automated gate.
- Narrow or remove the always-bypass actor unless it is an intentional recovery mechanism. Prefer a bypass policy that still requires a pull request.
- Enable strict required status checks / require branches to be up to date, or explicitly document why merge-base freshness is not required.
- Recheck these settings after any repository-policy change.

## Evidence
- Ruleset: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/rules/25836352
- PR #39 fix: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/39
- PR #39 merge commit: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/commit/541a633116ae6b2ff9361afcda139edd347d7136
- GitHub required-check troubleshooting: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks

The available GitHub integration can read rulesets but exposes no ruleset mutation action. This issue tracks the remaining settings and does not claim they have been changed.

## Update — 2026-10-26

- PR #40 merged: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/40 adds a regression contract ensuring `.github/workflows/security-audit-isolated.yml` runs on every pull request targeting `main` and has no `paths` / `paths-ignore` filter under `pull_request`. All 14 checks observed on its exact head SHA completed successfully.
- PR #41 merged: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/41 records the verified operational status and outstanding readiness gaps in `docs/STATUS_2026-10-26.md` and `docs/ROADMAP_STATUS_2026-10-26.md`.
- Main now points to `62ace31b4cdba42784c8439bc5a5b6e8a8100ca9`. At the last check, post-merge checks on this exact commit were still running; do not treat the prior commit's results or queued checks as a completed pass.
- No ruleset policy change is claimed. The bypass actor, zero required approvals, and loose freshness policy remain unresolved because the available GitHub integration exposes read access but no ruleset mutation action.
- Production readiness remains unproven: no verified 24/7 host, external alert delivery, or independent off-host backup/restore drill.


## Update — 2026-10-25 21:20 UTC

- PR #42 merged and PR #43 subsequently merged to reconcile `STATE.md` and `ROADMAP.md` with the observed repository state: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/42 and https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/43.
- Current `main` is `f1a179008ea093ebad205df81a958949faae28c2`. Post-merge checks for this exact commit were queued at the last observation; verify their final conclusions before treating the new commit as CI-validated.
- PR #43's relevant pull-request checks completed successfully before merge: tests, YAML validation, Gitleaks, offline regression/evaluator, Python static security analysis, dependency audit, Semgrep, and the aggregate security audit.
- The main ruleset policy itself has not been changed: repository-role bypass remains `always`, approvals remain zero, and strict freshness remains disabled. These require an authorized settings change, not a documentation-only PR.
- Runtime deployment, external alert delivery, and independent off-host restore remain unverified.


## Update — 2026-10-25 21:26 UTC

- PR #45 merged: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/45
- Added `scripts/check_detect_secrets.py` as the shared fail-closed gate for the `detect-secrets` report.
- Added an ephemeral synthetic canary test to the Python security workflow. The canary is generated at runtime in a temporary directory, detected successfully by `detect-secrets`, and the shared gate returned the expected rejection code. No real credential was used.
- On the exact PR head `c660c39f08531c8cdec98ded87c7959ee07b7c6a`, all observed checks passed: tests, YAML parsing, Gitleaks, offline regression/evaluator, Python SAST/secrets/dependency audit, Semgrep, static security analysis, dependency audit, and the additional offline benchmark suite.

- Remaining governance items are unchanged: bypass actor remains `always`, approvals remain zero, and strict status-check freshness remains disabled. Secret Scanning/Push Protection settings still cannot be confirmed through the currently available repository metadata.
- Production runtime, external alert delivery, and independent off-host backup/restore remain unverified.


## Update — 2026-10-25 21:28 UTC

On the observed PR head, tests, YAML parsing, Gitleaks, offline regression/evaluator, Python static security analysis, and Semgrep passed; dependency audit/security installation checks were still running. Do not merge until all checks on the exact head conclude successfully.

## Update — 2026-10-25 21:33 UTC

Secret Scanning/Push Protection settings cannot be confirmed from the public-repository alert endpoint alone (GitHub documents 404 for public repositories as well as disabled scanning).
- Still unverified: production host with 24/7 worker, external alert delivery, independent off-host backup and a tested restore, and live CLI cross-model quality comparison for Claudex Loop. PR #22 remains a draft and must not be merged as-is because it conflicts with the current security workflow and has no live quality evidence.


## Update — 2026-10-26 00:56 UTC

- PR #74 merged: https://github.com/ghith93/agent-team-starter/pull/74
- Main is now `232843716195d09a47fd2151db9c4f587de566ad`. Post-merge tests, offline regression, YAML validation, Gitleaks, Bandit/static analysis, Semgrep, dependency audit, and the Python secret-scanning gate all passed on this commit.

Part of #107 (ADR 0011). Continuous detection of people or agents getting around the gate:
- direct pushes that skip the gate
- approvals made outside the system
- branch protection, ruleset or policy edits
- token creation outside the broker
- bursts of rejected signatures
- rubber-stamping (approval latency, approve-without-open, canary requests)
- agents attempting guarded commands
- disabled or changed webhooks and apps
- a landed change that doesn't match the declared change
Alerts go to the audit trail and the incident automation (ADR 0007).

items.title: P0: Subagents bypass per-step approval (autonomousMode)
items.body:
## Summary
Delegated subagents are created with `autonomousMode = true`, and `AgentLoop` approves every step in autonomous mode without consulting the approval policy. A subagent can therefore execute tools that the parent run would have required the user to approve.

## Evidence
- `core/src/agent/AgentRuntime.cpp:949-954` — subagent config sets `autonomousMode = true`.
- `core/src/agent/AgentLoop.cpp:953-960` — autonomous mode synthesizes an `Approved` decision with the message "per-step approval is bypassed".
- The subagent tool allow-list is read-only today, but the bypass is a general loop behavior and does not depend on that allow-list.

## Impact
Approval is not transitive across delegation. A prompt that reaches a subagent can perform approved-class operations without a user prompt, and the run record attributes the action to the subagent rather than to an explicit grant.

## Proposed fix
- Inherit the parent run's approval policy and permission scope in subagents.
- If autonomous delegation is desired, require an explicit user grant that names the delegated capability set.
- Record the delegation and the inherited policy in the run trace.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A subagent cannot execute an approval-required tool without either an inherited decision or a new prompt.
- [ ] Autonomous delegation requires an explicit, scoped grant.
- [ ] Tests cover parent-approved, parent-denied and no-decision paths.


---
Phase: P0 · Source: 2026-10-22 gap analysis @ `d4bff5a2`

items.title: Require human approval before agent PRs merge
items.body:
## Why

CONTRIBUTING.md says agent PRs need a human's approval before they merge, at least until evals are strong enough to trust them. Nothing enforces that today: `main`'s branch protection requires signed commits but no reviews, and humans are allowed to self-merge.

## What

Make GitHub block an agent-authored PR from merging until a human approves it, without adding a review requirement to human PRs.

Options to compare:

- A ruleset or required status check that fails while a PR authored by the Satat GitHub App has no approving human review.
- Requiring reviews on all PRs and letting humans bypass. This is simpler, but it changes the self-merge rule.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An agent-authored PR cannot merge without a human approval
- [ ] A human-authored PR can still be self-merged
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md says how it's enforced
